title: Cap. 7 Scholastici open: Sed missis — Lombard sufficienter/efficaciter
pass_a_gloss: But the ancients having been set aside, let us descend to the Scholastics and modern Pontificians: who so defend Christ as having died for all, that they meanwhile acknowledge him as having died for the Elect alone with a special intention of applying his death to the same unto the infallible attainment of eternal life. 1. Let us begin from the Master of the Scholastics, Peter Lombard; Christ offered himself on the altar of the cross for all, as to the sufficiency of the price; but for the elect only, as to efficacy, because he effects salvation only for the predestined, book 3, distinction 20, letter c. The reason which the Master subjoins, why Christ is said to have died for the elect alone as to efficacy, is most worthy of observation. For he does not bring that which the Pelagians and Arminians would have brought, namely that they alone were foreseen, excited by grace according to the freedom of their choice, as going to apply Christ to themselves, but that in them alone by the kindness of his special mercy he effected salvation. But what he effected by his death in the Elect, he doubtless decreed to effect. And this is that special intention under which we profess Christ's death related and ordained to the elect alone.
pass_b_english: Setting the older writers aside, we come down to the Scholastics and modern Romanists. They defend Christ as having died for all, yet they also grant he died for the elect alone with a special intention to apply that death to them so that eternal life follows without fail. 1. Start with Peter Lombard, master of the Scholastics: Christ offered himself on the cross's altar for all as to the price's sufficiency, but for the elect only as to efficacy, because he effects salvation only for the predestined (Sentences 3, dist. 20, litt. c). The reason he gives for calling Christ's death efficacious for the elect alone is worth marking. He does not say what Pelagians and Arminians would say — that only those were foreseen who, stirred by grace in free choice, would apply Christ to themselves — but that in them alone, by the kindness of special mercy, he wrought salvation. What his death wrought in the elect he surely decreed to work. That is the special intention under which we say Christ's death is related and ordained to the elect alone.
source_text: Sed missis antiquioribus, ad Scholasticos & modernos Pontificios descendamus: Qui sic defendunt Christum pro omnibus mortuum, ut interim agnoscant pro Electis solis mortuum cum speciali intentione mortem suam eisdem applicandi ad infallibilem consecutionem vitae aeternae. 1. Ordiamur a Magistro Scholasticorum Petro Lombardo; Christus se in ara crucis obtulit pro omnibus, quantum ad pretii sufficientiam; sed pro electis tantum, quantum ad efficaciam, quia praedestinatis tantum salutem efficit, lib. 3. dist. 20 litt. c. Ratio quam subnectit Magister, cur Christus pro solis electis mortuus dicatur quantum ad efficaciam, est observatione dignissima. Non enim illam affert quam Pelagiani & Arminiani attulissent, scilicet quod illi tantum praevidebantur, pro libertate arbitrii sui per gratiam excitati, ut Christum sibi applicaturi, sed quod in illis tantum pro benignitate specialis suae misericordiae salutem effecerit. Quod autem morte sua in Electis effecit, proculdubio efficere decrevit. Atque haec est illa specialis intentio sub qua mortem Christi ad solos electos relatam, & ordinatam profitemur.
